page: Microsoft Azure D96ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on x86_64 architecture and powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. The configuration allocates 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at up to 3.7 GHz. Cache architecture includes 32 KB L1 data, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. Memory stands at 384.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Modern instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, alongside AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic support.

Integrated hardware includes 5670 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, providing substantial low-latency ephemeral disk capacity directly attached to the hypervisor without consuming remote storage throughput. The instance includes no discrete graphics processing units. In synthetic stress-ng benchmarks, the system demonstrated strong single-core CPU execution (score 3077.28, placing in the top 25%) and top-tier multi-core capability (score 147458.16, placing in the top 10%). It also registered strong throughput in in-memory workloads, sustaining 113.08 million Redis SET operations per second.

Cost efficiency is driven by high core density and bundled high-capacity NVMe storage, which eliminates additional provisioning fees for local scratch and caching tiers. The balanced compute-to-memory profile makes the D96ads_v6 suited for demanding enterprise workloads including distributed relational databases, heavy analytics, batch data processing, and large-scale web services requiring fast ephemeral storage.
